questions.q: What is the number of ways in which an examiner can assign 10 marks to 4 questions, giving not less than 2 marks to any questions?
questions.solution: $x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}+x_{4}=10 \quad x_{i} \geq 2\Rightarrow\left(x_{1}-2\right)+\left(x_{2}-2\right)+\left(x_{3}-2\right)+\left(x_{4}-2\right)=2\begin{array}{llll}\mathrm{y}_{1} & \mathrm{y}_{2} & \mathrm{y}_{3} & \mathrm{y}_{4}\end{array} \mathrm{y}_{1}+\mathrm{y}_{2}+\mathrm{y}_{3}+\mathrm{y}_{4}=$2 ; $\mathrm{y}_{i} \geq$0\therefore$ N.O.W $={ }^{2+4-1} $\mathrm{C}_{4-1}={ }^{5} \mathrm{C}_{3}=$10
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main

questions.q: A round table conference is to be held amongst 20 countries. If two particular delegates wish to sit together, then such arrangements can be done in ways.
questions.solution: We consider two particular delegates as single unit now 19 units can be arranged around a round table in 18! ways and the two delegates can be arranged mutually in 2 ! ways Hence the required number of ways is $2 \times(18$ !)

questions.q: A person invites a party of 10 friends at dinner and place them so that 4 are on one round table and 6 on the other round table. The number of ways in which he can arrange the guests is
questions.solution:
Selection of 6 guests $=10 \mathrm{C} 6$
Permutation of 6 on round table $=5 !$
Permutation of 4 on round table $=3 !$
Then, total number of arrangements $=10 \mathrm{C} 6.5 ! .3 !$
$=\frac{(10) !}{6 ! 4 !} \cdot 5 ! .3 !=\frac{(10) !}{24}$

questions.q: The teacher wants to arrange 5 students on the platform such that the boy $\mathrm{B}_1$ occupies second position and the girls $\mathrm{G}_1$ and $\mathrm{G}_2$ are always adjacent to each other, then the number of such arrangements is
questions.solution: There are 5 positions. Given that $\mathrm{B}_1$ occupies $2^{\text {nd }}$ position $\therefore \quad \mathrm{B}_1$ can be arranged in 1 way. As $G_1$ and $G_2$ are always together, none of them can take $1^{\text {st }}$ position. $\therefore \quad \mathrm{G}_1, \mathrm{G}_2$ and one of the remaining students can be arranged on $3^{\text {rd }}, 4^{\text {th }}$ and $5^{\text {th }}$ position when $\mathrm{G}_1$ and $\mathrm{G}_2$ are always together in $2 ! \times 2$ ! Ways. And remaining 2 students can be arranged in 2 ! Ways. $\therefore \quad$ The required number of arrangements $\begin{aligned} & =2 ! \times 2 ! \times 2 ! \\ & =8 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If all possible numbers are formed by using the digits $1, 2, 3, 5, 7$ without repetition and they are arranged in descending order, then the rank of the number $327$ is
questions.solution:
Given numbers are& $1, 2, 3, 5, 7$.

And also they are arranged in descending order.

i.e., the numbers with four and five digits are included.

The number of five-digit number$= 5 !$

The number of four digits number

$= p4 5 = \dfrac{5 !}{( 5 - 4 ) !} = \dfrac{120}{1} = 120$

The number of $3$ digits starting with $7 =$

i.e., $4$ digits have to be fit in $2$ place in $p2 4$~ways,

$p2 4 = \dfrac{4 !}{( 4 - 2 ) !} = 4 \times 3 = 12$

The number of $3$ digits numbers starting with $5 =$

$p2 4 = \dfrac{4 !}{( 4 - 2 ) !} = 4 \times 3 = 12$

The number of digits starting with $3$

i.e., $3$ numbers have to fit in $1$ place in $p1 3$ way.

$p1 3 = \dfrac{3 !}{( 3 - 1 ) !} = \dfrac{3 \times 2 \times 1}{2 \times 1} = 3 = 3$

The number of digits starting with $\mathop{3}_{¯}\mathop{5}_{¯}$~is,

$p1 3 = \dfrac{3 !}{( 3 - 1 ) !} = \dfrac{3 \times 2 \times 1}{2 \times 1} = 3$

And the next number is $327$.

$∴$ The rank of $327$ is

$= 120 + 120 + 12 + 12 + 3 + 3 + 1$

$= 271$

$∴$ Rank of $327 = 271$

questions.q: If a polygon of $n$ sides has 275 diagonals, then $n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
A polygon of $n$ sides has number of diagonals
$=\frac{n(n-3)}{2}=275 \quad$ (given)
$\begin{array}{cc}\Rightarrow& n²-3 n-550=0 \\ \Rightarrow & n²-25 n+22 n-550=0 \\ \Rightarrow & n(n-25)+22(n-25)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & (n-25)(n+22)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & n=25,(\because n=-22 \text { is not possible })\end{array}$

questions.solution:
$8 \le p + q + r \le 12$
$⇒ p + q + r = 8,9, 10,11,12$
Here, $p, q, r \ge 1$
Hence, required number {using number of positive integral solutions = ${}^{n - 1}{C}_{r - 1}$ }
$= {}^{7}{C}_{2} + {}^{8}{C}_{2} + {}^{9}{C}_{2} + {}^{10}{C}_{2} + {}^{11}{C}_{2}$
$= \dfrac{7 \times 6}{2} + \dfrac{8 \times 7}{2} + \dfrac{9 \times 8}{2} + \dfrac{10 \times 9}{2} + \dfrac{11 \times 10}{2}$
$= 21 + 28 + 36 + 45 + 55$
$= 185$

questions.q: For $N = 12600$, the number of even divisors is
questions.solution:
On prime factorization we have,& $N = 12600 = {2}^{3}{3}^{2}{5}^{2}{7}^{1}$.

Number of factors~$= \left(3 + 1\right)\left(2 + 1\right)\left(2 + 1\right)\left(1 + 1\right) = 72 .$

Removing power of~$2$~remaining factors which are odd~$= \left(2 + 1\right)\left(2 + 1\right)\left(1 + 1\right) = 18 .$

~$∴$ Even factors $= 72 - 18 = 54 .$

Hence, the answer is~$54 .$
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main

questions.q: If $t_n$ denotes the number of triangles formed with $n$ points in a plane, no three of which are collinear and if $t_{n+1}-t_n=36$, then $n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$t_n=$ The number of triangles formed with $n$ points in a plane, no three of which are collinear.
i.e., $\begin{aligned}$& t_n={ }^n C_3 \\
& t_{n+1}={ }^{n+1} C_3
\end{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad t_{n+1}={ }^{n+1} C_3 Now, $t_{n+1}-t_n=36\begin{array}{crrl}
\Rightarrow$& { }^{n+1} C_3-{ }^n C_3=36 \\
\Rightarrow & $\frac{(n+1) !}{(n-2) ! 3 !}-\frac{n !}{(n-3) ! 3 !}=$36 \\
\Rightarrow & $\frac{(n+1) n(n-1)}{6}-\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}=$36 \\
\Rightarrow & & n(n-1)(n+1-n+2)=36 $\times$6 \\
\Rightarrow & & 3 n(n-1)=36 $\times$6 \\
\Rightarrow & & n²-n-72=0 \\
\Rightarrow & & n²-9 n+8 n-72=0 \\
\Rightarrow & & n(n-9)+8(n-9)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & & (n-9)(n+8)=0 \\
\therefore & & n=9 \quad(\because n $\neq-$3)
\end{array}

questions.q:
Consider the following statements
$i$. Number of ways of placing $' n '$objects in $k$ bins $k \le n$ ) such that no bin is empty is $Ck - 1 ( n - 1 )$

$ii$. Number of ways of writing a positive integer " $n$ ' into a sum of $k$ positive integers is $Ck - 1 ( n - 1 )$

$iii$. Number of ways of placing ' $n$ ' objects in $k$ bins such that at least~one bin is non-empty is $Ck - 1 ( n - 1 )$

$iv$. $Ck n - Ck n - 1 = Ck - 1 ( n - 1 )$
questions.solution:
\left(i\right)$. Number of ways of placing $' n '$objects in $k$ bins $k \le n$ ) such that no bin is empty is equal to number of integral solution of~

${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} + . . . + {x}_{k} = n$

which is

$= Ck - 1 n - 1$

\left(ii\right)$~Let

${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} + . . . + {x}_{k} = n$

Then, number of positive integral solutions are

$= Ck - 1 n - 1$

\left(iii\right)$. Number of ways of placing ' $n$ ' objects in $k$ bins such that at least~one bin is non-empty is equal to the number of non-negative integrals solution of

${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} + . . . + {x}_{k} = n$

which is~$= Ck - 1 n + k - 1$

\left(iv\right)$

$Ck n - Ck n - 1 = Ck - 1 ( n - 1 )$

\left[∵ Ck n = \dfrac{n !}{( n - r ) ! r !}\right]$

$\text{LHS}$

$= \dfrac{n !}{( n - k ) ! k !} - \dfrac{( n - 1 ) !}{( n - k - 1 ) ! k !}$

$= \dfrac{n !}{\left(n - k\right) \cdot \left(n - k - 1\right) ! \cdot k !} - \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right) !}{\left(n - k - 1\right) ! \cdot k !}$

$= \dfrac{n ! - \left(n - k\right)\left(n - 1\right) !}{\left(n - k\right) \cdot \left(n - k - 1\right) ! \cdot k !}$

$= \dfrac{n \cdot \left(n - 1\right) ! - \left(n - k\right)\left(n - 1\right) !}{\left(n - k\right) \cdot \left(n - k - 1\right) ! \cdot k !}$

$= \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right) ! \left[n - \left(n - k\right)\right]}{\left(n - k\right) \cdot \left(n - k - 1\right) ! \cdot k !}$

$= \dfrac{k \cdot \left(n - 1\right) !}{\left(n - k\right) \cdot \left(n - k - 1\right) ! \cdot k !}$

$= \dfrac{k \cdot \left(n - 1\right) !}{\left(n - k\right) \cdot \left(n - k - 1\right) ! \cdot k \cdot \left(k - 1\right) !}$

$= \dfrac{( n - 1 ) !}{( n - k ) ! ( k - 1 ) !} = Ck - 1 n - 1$

$

questions.q: The total number of ways in which $5$ balls of different colours can be distributed among $3$ persons such that each person gets at least one ball is
questions.solution:
We know that total number of ways of distributing $n$ distinct things among $m$ persons such that each person gets at least one thing

$= m^{n} - C m {}_{1} . {( m - 1 )}^{n} + C m {}_{2} {( m - 2 )}^{n} - C m {}_{3} {( m - 3 )}^{n} + .....$

So the required total number of ways

$= {3}^{5} - C 3 {}_{1} {.2}^{5} + C 3 {}_{2} {.1}^{5}$ .

$= 243 - 96 + 3$

$= 150$

questions.q: How many numbers can be made with the help of the digits $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ which are greater than~$3000$ (repetition is not allowed)
questions.solution:
All the $5$ digit numbers and $6$ digit numbers are greater than $3000$. Therefore, number of 5 digit numbers $= { }^{6}{P}_{5} - { }^{5}{P}_{5} = 600$.

{Since the case that $0$ will be at ten thousand place should be subtracted}.

Similarly, number of $6$ digit numbers $6 ! - 5 ! = 600$.

Now, the numbers of~$4$~digit numbers which are greater than~$3000$, having $3$, $4$ or $5$ at first place, this can be done in $3$ ways and remaining~$3$ digit may be filled from remaining $5$ digits i.e. required number of $4$ digit numbers are${}^{5}{P}_{3} \times 3 = 180$ .

Hence, total numbers~$= 600 + 600 + 180 = 1380$
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main
